payload.title: Greece Wedding Packages and What They Include
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning 60 to 150 guests flying in from Australia. They have settled on Greece, have two or three venues in mind and are now holding package documents that look alike but are not: one bundles legal paperwork and a ceremony, another sells exclusive use of a terrace, a third needs a planner. They want to know what a Greek venue package really covers, what sits outside it and how to put two quotes side by side before they commit a deposit.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can compare the couple's shortlisted Greek venue packages like for like, with inclusions confirmed in writing and the quote in AUD.
payload.angle: Greek venue packages share a name but not a shape. Some resorts sell a ceremony bundle with legal paperwork and a coordinator (Elounda Beach's indicative package, Elounda Peninsula's separate civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic packages); some publish named tiers (Nana Princess); some sell exclusive use of a space and leave the rest to a planner (Grace Hotel); others set minimum guest counts, room blocks or nights as package conditions (Abaton, Elounda Peninsula, Melenos). Page-one results list prices and adjectives; this guide shows, venue by venue and only from what each venue publishes about its own package, what sits inside, what sits outside, and turns the gaps into a like-for-like checklist an Australian couple can take into any quote. No figures, so the comparison stays true when prices change.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: a Greek venue wedding package usually bundles the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and some paperwork, while guest rooms, exclusive use, transfers and outside suppliers vary by venue; link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues prominently and the hub /destinations/europe/greece.
Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways, no figures.
What a Greek venue package usually includes: each inclusion tied to the venue that publishes it (batch A and B venues), written in fresh wording.

Ceremony type inside a package: civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic, with legal meaning only as Embassy Athens, Smartraveller or the venue states it; link the Greece guide's legal section; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once.

What packages often leave out, written as questions and only where a venue states it: exclusive-use hire, guest rooms and minimum nights, transfers, extra hours, outside suppliers, document fees ('a fee applies' only where the source says so).
Venue package vs a planner vs building your own: practical trade-offs, no competitor or planner names, Advisor claims from brand-facts.md only.

How to compare two quotes like for like: a checklist (ceremony type, guest count basis, spaces and hours, exclusive use, rooms and nights, transfers, supplier rules, documents, currency, deposit and cancellation terms), no figures.
Australian angle: what currency the quote is in, deposit and cancellation terms as questions, Smartraveller travel insurance advice (dated once).

FAQ (4 to 6): Are Greek wedding packages all inclusive? Does a package include the legal paperwork? Can we bring our own planner or suppliers? Do we need to book guest rooms to get a package? Can Australians legally marry in Greece?

Links: /destination-wedding-packages and /destination-packages prominently if SEO confirms relevance; /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues; /expert-advice/what-is-included-in-lake-como-wedding-packages if natural; /magazine as the magnet; /wonderland-concierge after the comparison checklist and at the close. UTMs ?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing.
avoid: Any price, fee, euro or AUD figure, 'from' price or percentage anywhere, including FAQ and meta.

Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, trace or confirm; sources or method; 'you will often read'; myths sections); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once.
Stating a legal meaning or custom origin not in an official source; any Advisor role in legal, church or religious paperwork.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, review sites or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images.
Planner or other vendor names (venue names only where their package is described); venue contact details; implied partnerships or preferred rates.
Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; 'from first idea to the last dance', 'last dance'.
Ranking packages as 'best'; implying a package is all inclusive unless the venue says so.
Clichés, exclamation marks, pasted keywords or bracketed keywords in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.
Any change to content/posts/italy-wedding-packages or the live site.
payload.cannibalisation_check: No existing page is an editorial explainer on Greek venue packages. Overlaps: /destination-wedding-packages ('All-Inclusive Destination Wedding Packages', commercial, includes Santorini) and /destination-packages (commercial, includes Santorini) could rank for package terms; the hub /destinations/europe/greece (venue-led, links to the packages edit). /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues and /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues (drafts) own venue intent; /all-inclusive-wedding-cost is cost intent; /expert-advice/what-is-included-in-lake-como-wedding-packages is the Italy sister explainer. This post owns the 'what is inside a Greek package and how to compare' intent and links prominently to the commercial pages if SEO finds one ranking; the run report recommends the keyword split. No live page changes.
payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's real problem (two Greek package documents that look alike but are not), give the direct answer in the first 100 words, then link the Greece venues guide and the hub.
key_takeaways_plan: A Greek venue package usually covers the ceremony, its set-up and a coordinator, and the rest depends on the venue.
Civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic ceremonies are often packaged separately, so check which one a package is built for.
Exclusive use, guest rooms, transfers and outside suppliers are where packages differ most, so ask about each in writing.
Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before paying any deposit.
